extracted.intended_audience: health insurers, health plans, Medicaid programs, third-party administrators, benefits designers, regulators, and other covered entities and stakeholders subject to Section 1557
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing, administering, and evaluating health insurance coverage and other health-related benefit designs for compliance with Section 1557 nondiscrimination requirements, including investigative and defense frameworks OCR will apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental alteration defense for integration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A program is not required to provide coverage for a service in the most integrated setting appropriate to an individual's needs if it would fundamentally alter the program to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR clarifies the availability of the fundamental alteration defense as written in the rule and declines to incorporate further specification; commenters asked whether an Olmstead integration plan is required to raise this defense and for guidance incorporating DOJ ADA Title II case law, but OCR did not adopt prescriptive text here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimate, nondiscriminatory reason defense and pretext review
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities may defend a challenged action or practice by providing a legitimate, nondiscriminatory reason for their actions that is not pretext for discrimination; OCR will evaluate whether the reason is pretextual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will consider whether a denial or limitation of a health service is based on unlawful animus or bias or is a pretext for discrimination, and will scrutinize asserted nondiscriminatory reasons (e.g., medical necessity or other medical management techniques) to determine if they are genuine. Covered entities can submit any legitimate reason, but OCR may investigate further.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of McDonnell Douglas and Arlington Heights frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR will rely on general nondiscrimination principles and longstanding civil rights case law including Arlington Heights and the McDonnell Douglas burden-shifting framework when evaluating claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arlington Heights is used to evaluate multiple types of evidence that collectively show discriminatory intent; McDonnell Douglas is an inferential burden-shifting method for circumstantial evidence cases—these frameworks apply to circumstantial evidence cases but not where there is direct evidence (e.g., a facially discriminatory policy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissibility of medical necessity and reasonable medical management
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities are not prohibited from employing reasonable medical management techniques, including medical necessity, when applied in a neutral, nondiscriminatory manner and not otherwise prohibited by Federal or State law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR is revising regulatory text to reference reasonable medical management techniques, including medical necessity. When assessing whether actions are discriminatory or nondiscriminatory, OCR will review whether medical necessity determinations are bona fide medical judgments supported by clinical, evidence-based criteria, not conduct a general review of the medical judgment itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and documentation OCR may request for medical necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR may require a covered entity to provide its medical necessity standards, clinical evidence-based criteria or guidelines relied upon, and the medical substantiation for a medical necessity determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will evaluate whether a medical necessity rationale is bona fide and may treat determinations not based on clinical, evidence-based criteria as evidence of pretext for discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissibility and limits on utilization management techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilization management techniques such as prior authorization, step therapy (fail-first), and durational or quantity limits are permissible if applied in a neutral, nondiscriminatory manner and not otherwise prohibited by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR expects such tools to be developed and applied neutrally; guidelines should be applied consistently with clinical standards across patient populations to ensure equal clinical treatment across protected bases. Excessive use targeting a particular condition that could be a disability could violate Section 1557.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of potentially excessive or discriminatory medical management
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices commenters identified as potentially excessive: requiring step therapy for new enrollees already on a working treatment; transferring management of medicines to niche vendors with more extensive controls; requiring off-label meds within step therapy; imposing categorical prior authorization/step therapy requirements on most or all drugs for a disease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR acknowledges these as examples commenters suggested of potentially discriminatory or excessive utilization management and will consider such factual patterns in case-by-case analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: No per se list of discriminatory benefit design practices
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR declines to state in rule or preamble that specific benefit design practices (e.g., drug tiering, utilization management) are per se discriminatory under Section 1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinations will be made in a fact-specific, case-by-case inquiry considering the plan as a whole, consistency of neutral criteria, and other relevant factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs and extraordinary costs as potential nondiscriminatory justifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities may assert costs, including extraordinary costs, as legitimate nondiscriminatory reasons for certain benefit designs, but cost savings alone cannot justify designs that disfavor coverage of medically necessary services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR recognizes issuers need flexibility to address high-cost items (e.g., novel gene therapies) but warns against using cost justifications to mask discriminatory designs; OCR will scrutinize such defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency expectations and OCR authority to request plan information
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR encourages issuers to disclose coverage details, utilization management practices, denial rates, and reasons for denials and has authority to request such information from covered entities when necessary to determine compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR considered but declined to impose a blanket disclosure requirement; nonetheless, it stresses its power to request data and cautions that lack of transparency can impede detection of discrimination. Appeals processes that impose excessive administrative burdens on protected individuals may be discriminatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discriminatory use of value assessment methods (e.g., QALYs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of value assessment methods that penalize patients or groups on a protected ground (race, color, national origin, age, disability, sex) and thereby limit access to aids, benefits, or services may violate Section 1557; methods that discount life-extension value on the basis of disability or age are impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR notes proposed rulemaking under Section 504 also targets discriminatory discounting in value assessment; OCR will evaluate any value assessment methodology for discriminatory application rather than rule on specific measures at this time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to develop inclusive value assessment metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR and commenters urged development of new value assessment measures that incorporate input from patients with disabilities (and family members and providers) and address cultural barriers to adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR supports research and dissemination of methodologies and notes NIH and NIDILRR initiatives and other Department research priorities that align with this goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall benefit design analysis approach (case-by-case, plan-as-a-whole)
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR will apply basic nondiscrimination principles and civil rights case law to the specific facts of a plan's benefit design, considering the plan as a whole, whether similar limitations apply to other services, and whether neutral, nondiscriminatory criteria are consistently relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered entities have the opportunity to articulate legitimate nondiscriminatory justifications which OCR will scrutinize for pretext; OCR may investigate whether cited medical standards are evidence-based and not merely a single literature citation used to shield discriminatory design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to provide covered services neutrally if offered
rubrics_metrics.description: While the rule does not require a covered entity to provide coverage for a particular health service, to the extent a covered entity provides coverage for a particular health service, it must provide the health service to all individuals in a neutral, nondiscriminatory manner consistent with the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This emphasizes nondiscriminatory administration of benefits offered, not imposition of specific coverage mandates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with other Federal and State regulators — non-determinative compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with other State or Federal laws or plan regulators (e.g., CMS requirements for EHB, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid) is relevant but not determinative of compliance with Section 1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will coordinate with other agencies to avoid inconsistency and duplication, will consider overlapping requirements, but as lead enforcement agency it retains sole authority to determine compliance with this final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability of multiple entities and responsibility for subcontractors
rubrics_metrics.description: Where multiple covered entities provide or administer elements of a discriminatory benefit design, all such entities (including third-party administrators, benefits advisers, consultants, subrecipients, subcontractors) may be found liable under Section 1557; direct recipients and subrecipients are both responsible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered entities cannot outsource or contract away civil rights obligations; OCR discussed responsibility of third party administrators and will treat participating entities as potentially liable.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR investigative posture and remedies (complaint-driven and proactive tools)
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR investigates alleged discrimination via complaint investigations and compliance reviews and will publish resolution agreements and press releases to inform best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR acknowledges its process tends to review existing plans but emphasizes consistent investigatory approach. OCR will employ all available means, may request plan documents and clinical criteria, and may use published resolutions to educate covered entities; OCR declines to provide a prescriptive safe harbor at this time.
